## Verdict

**Inkwell** costs least for a team of 22, at **$242 per month**. Its 20-seat minimum sits below the team size, so all 22 seats bill at the list rate of $11 with no padding. Dorado is next at $528, and Borealis is the most expensive at $600 despite a mid-range per-seat rate, because its 40-seat minimum forces payment for 18 unused seats.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $24 | 5 |
| Inkwell | $11 | 20 |
| Borealis | $15 | 40 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 22 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Dorado:** minimum 5 < 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $24 = **$528 per month**. Effective rate $24.00 per person.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 20 < 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $11 = **$242 per month**. Effective rate $11.00 per person.
- **Borealis:** minimum 40 > 22, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Effective rate $27.27 per person ($600 ÷ 22); 18 seats worth $270 go unused.

Inkwell is $286 per month cheaper than Dorado and $358 per month cheaper than Borealis — $3,432 and $4,296 per year.

## Risks

Inkwell's lead is tight against its own floor. At 20 people or fewer it still bills $220, so the effective rate climbs if the team shrinks; Dorado's 5-seat minimum makes it the more forgiving option for a contracting team, though at $24 per seat it only undercuts Inkwell's $220 floor below 10 people.

Borealis's penalty is purely a minimum-seat artefact. Its $600 is fixed until 40 users, at which point the effective rate drops to $15 — still above Inkwell's $11, so Borealis does not overtake Inkwell on list price at any size.

This compares price only. The list carries no detail on features, support tiers, usage limits, or security, so a cheaper seat may buy less product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, negotiated discounts, onboarding and migration costs are not in the source and could change the ranking.
